summary: EU, UK and ECOWAS citizens (among others) enter Cabo Verde visa-free, many other nationalities can obtain a tourist visa on arrival for CVE 5,000 (about EUR 45), and since 1 January 2026 nationals of 91 listed countries need a visa from an embassy before travel, but every traveler must pre-register on the official EASE platform and pay the airport security tax before flying.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Cabo Verde?
faq.answer: EU, UK and several other European citizens enter visa-free for up to 30 days, as do US, Canadian, Chinese and other nationalities on the government's visa-exemption list, and ECOWAS citizens enter freely. Many other nationalities can obtain a tourist visa on arrival at international airports for CVE 5,000 (about EUR 45), or CVE 2,500 if requested in advance on EASE. Since 1 January 2026, nationals of 91 countries on the government's list must get a visa from a Cabo Verde embassy before travel, including for transit. Everyone must pre-register on the EASE platform first.

faq.question: What is the EASE registration and the airport tax?
faq.answer: EASE (ease.gov.cv) is Cabo Verde's official pre-registration platform. Before flying, every international traveler registers their trip and pays the airport security tax (TSA) of 3,400 escudos — about EUR 31. Airlines check the confirmation at check-in.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Cabo Verde?
faq.answer: Up to 30 days visa-free under the EU–Cabo Verde arrangement in force since 2019. Longer stays require an extension from immigration in Cabo Verde or a visa from an embassy before travel.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccine for Cabo Verde?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, such as much of mainland West Africa. Direct arrivals from Europe or the Americas do not need the certificate.
